newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Berisha proposes relax curfew in Albania north.
newsitem.headline: Berisha proposes relax curfew in Albania north.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha on Wednesday proposed relaxing a nationwide curfew, one of the measures introduced as part of state of emergency after the outbreak of armed rebellion in the south of the country.

The president called for the hours of the dusk-to-dawn curfew to be shortened in the north and central part of Albania to between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m. (2100 and 0500 GMT), Albanian state television quoted the presidential office as saying.

But the original curfew hours of 8 p.m. to 7 a.m. (1900 to 0600 GMT) should be maintained for southern regions of the Balkan state, covering the prefectures of Vlore, Gjirokaster, Fier and Berat, the president's office said.
The relaxation of the curfew hours was proposed by the president due to "a significant improvement of the situation", the office said.
The proposal by Berisha would be passed on to the Council of Defence for its stamp of approval.
Weeks of protests against Berisha and his government escalated into violent unrest across the south on Saturday and Sunday as rioters broke into police and army depots to seize guns and ammunition.

One of the biggest troublespots was in the Adriatic port of Vlore where at least 19 people were reported killed at the weekend. Albanian army soldiers and insurgents battled near Sarande on Wednesday after troops and police pushed south to try to crush the uprising.
